claims.text: In \(H^*(\mathrm{Gr}_{r,n})\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\), \(\Lambda\) has integral Schur basis and \(I_{r,n-r}\) is spanned by \(s_\lambda\) outside \((n-r)^r\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 213-218]

groundings.excerpt:
213: Let $\Lambda=\Lambda(x_1,x_2,\ldots)$ be the ring of symmetric functions with integral coefficients. This space has a ${\mathbb Z}$-linear basis consisting of \emph{Schur functions} $s_{\lambda}$,
214: where $\lambda$ is an integer partition. Consider the ideal
215: \[I_{r,n-r} = \mathrm{Span}_\mathbb{Z}\left\{s_\lambda\mid \lambda\nsubseteq (n-r)^r \right\} \]
216: of $\Lambda$. Then one has the following standard presentation of the cohomology of Grassmannians:
217: \[H^*(\mathrm{Gr}_{r,n})\cong \Lambda/I_{r,n-r}. \]
218: We will use an overline to denote the projection $\Lambda\to\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}$. Specifically, we will write $\overline{\Lambda}$ as a shorthand for $\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}$. We will also distinguish between $s_{\lambda}\in \Lambda$, the usual Schur function, and $\overline{s}_{\lambda}$ for its image in $\overline{\Lambda}$.

claims.text: For \(v_{r,s,t,n}\), with \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), the 2024 theorem proves minimality of \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 219-235]
RWY proves that the lower-adjoined and right-adjoined families generate \(J_v\) integrally; each has \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) elements. [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 864-892]

865: Given a bigrassmannian v=v_{r,s,t,n} in type A_{n-1} with \mathfrak{S}_{v}=s_{i^{j}}, let
866: \displaystyle a

872: (4.5)
873: \{s_{\mu}:i^{j}\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^{b},i^{j-b})\}.
874: Alternatively, J_{v} is generated by

877: We delay our proof of Theorem 4.8 until Section 4.7 .
878: Note that in both of the asserted generating sets ( 4.5 ) and ( 4.6 ) for J_{v},
879: the shapes \mu indexing the generators s_{\mu} run through an interval between
880: the j\times i rectangular shape i^{j} and the disjoint union of i^{j} with a
881: smaller rectangle of shape a\times b or b\times a.
882: In ( 4.5 ) the smaller rectangle is to the right
883: of the rectangle i^{j}, with both top-justified, while in ( 4.6 ) the
884: smaller rectangle is below the rectangle i^{j}, with both left-justified.
885: Thus in both cases, the generating sets have size \binom{a+b}{a}
886: and consist of generators whose multiset of degrees
887: have generating function
888: \sum_{\mu}q^{|\mu|}=q^{ij}\left[\begin{matrix}a+b\\
889: a\end{matrix}\right]_{q},
890: where \left[\begin{matrix}a+b\\
891: a\end{matrix}\right]_{q} is a q- binomial coefficient or Gaussian polynomial
